Clotrimazole reduces the levels or effects of streptomycin by influencing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of tacrolimus via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce tadalafil clearance, leading to increased systemic exposure and a higher risk of adverse events. Monitor closely. 6. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce zanubrutinib dosage to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 15. Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of alvimopan via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance is unknown. 16. Clotrimazole reduces amikacin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 17. Amobarbital decreases clotrimazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 18. Clotrimazole reduces the levels or effects of armodafinil via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance is unknown. 19. Clotrimazole reduces mestranol effects by increasing its metabolism, which may also cause menstrual irregularities. The clinical significance is unknown. 27. Clotrimazole decreases neomycin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 28. Clotrimazole decreases paromomycin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Pentobarbital decreases clotrimazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Phenobarbital decreases clotrimazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Clotrimazole decreases tobramycin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 34. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of atogepant by other mechanisms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The recommended dosage of atogepant with OATP inhibitors is 10 mg or 30 mg once daily. 35. Clotrimazole decreases atorvastatin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter but increases its toxicity through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 36. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of avanafil by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce avanafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and associated adverse events. The maximum recommended dose of avanafil is 50 mg, not to exceed once every 24 hours for patients taking moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Clotrimazole increases axitinib levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely and reduce the dose as necessary. 38. Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 42. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of estradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 43. Clotrimazole increases elagolix levels through other mechanisms. Concomitant use of elagolix and strong OATP1B1 inhibitors is contraindicated. 51. Clotrimazole increases eliglustat levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are not recommended with eliglustat poor or intermediate metabolizers. Reduce eliglustat dose to 84 mg once daily in extensive metabolizers. 52. Clotrimazole increases entrectinib levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. 53. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of finerenone by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 58. Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Clotrimazole increases the toxicity of fluvastatin through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 60. Reduce geprione dose by 50% when used concomitantly with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 61. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution when co-administering glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with OATP1B1/OATP1B3 inhibitors. 62. When co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the ibrutinib dose to 280 mg daily (for B-cell malignancies) or 420 mg daily (for graft-versus-host disease). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 67. Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism.
